why: The engine doctor has no concept of an accepted historical divergence, so every run re-reports the same findings and `ok` can never be true. This baseline records which divergences were already reviewed, so the doctor becomes a 'what is new' signal instead of a permanent red light. Scope is deliberately per-milestone: a code that also fires for live work keeps firing there.
limitations: The engine persists only a sample of its findings (10 issues of ~93 observed errors), so comparison is best-effort over that sample, never a complete reconciliation.
Entries are keyed by code plus milestone, extracted from recorded message text. A divergence whose message carries no milestone id is never suppressed.

This file is read by the governor control-plane check only. It does not change the engine doctor's own exit status, which stays `ok=false` until the divergence is repaired or the baseline is made engine-aware.
